key_insight: The paper shows that combining data storytelling with interpretable machine learning can make AI decisions understandable to non-experts without exposing sensitive data or model internals.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for deploying explainable AI in decision-support systems where transparency, accessibility, and data privacy must all be balanced.
method: Defines data storytelling for interpretable machine learning using the DIST Pyramid.
Introduces an I-P-O model and an architecture for "What-if" and "Why-not" explanation generation.
Uses data desensitization plus SHAP and LLMs to produce ABT-formatted stories.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with higher accessibility than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful story generation and desensitization, so preserving explanation fidelity while avoiding leakage of sensitive information is a key implementation concern.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
